Package frc.robot

Class RobotStateMachine

java.lang.Object
frc.robot.RobotStateMachine
public final class RobotStateMachine extends Object
Singleton that owns the robot's state, pose, aiming pipeline, and field-zone tracking.

Why a Singleton?

Many subsystems and commands need access to the same robot pose and aim state (drive, vision, turret, shooter, auto). A singleton eliminates the need to pass references through every constructor and keeps the shared state in one place. The instance is created eagerly at class load time (see instance) so there is no thread-safety risk from lazy initialization.

Aiming Pipeline

The full shot-computation chain runs on-demand via getAimParams(): 
   getAimParams()
     â†’ LeadCompensator.computeLeadTarget(hub, turretPose, fieldVelocity, m_tofAim)
         â†’ m_tofAim.update(virtualTarget, turretPose, kZero)   [15-iter convergence]
         â†’ AimParams { yaw, pitch, output, tof }
     â†’ m_tofAim.update(virtualTarget, turretPose, kZero)       [final params]
     â†’ AimParams (used by Turret.track and Shooter.shoot)

Periodic Structure

periodic() has two tiers:
  • Every loop (50 Hz): pose update, field-zone check, turret pose calculation. These feed directly into the 20 ms control loop and must run each cycle.
  • 10 Hz (rate-limited by m_telemetryTimer): SmartDashboard writes, NT4 struct publishes, LED color updates. Slower SmartDashboard writes reduce NT4 bandwidth and prevent loop overruns (see Stage 0 for the overrun history).

LED / Color State Machine

The getState() method implements a schedule-driven LED pattern based on the match timer and game-specific data from the Driver Station. Red flashes, green flashes, and solid colors signal alliance-specific scoring windows to the drive team.

    • getAimParams

      public AimParams getAimParams()
      Runs the full aiming pipeline and returns the current lead-compensated shot parameters.

      Called every loop by:

      • Shooter.tracked() (polled by the WPILib scheduler via the Trigger)
      • Turret.track() (inside the tracking run() command)
      • periodic() at 10 Hz for SmartDashboard telemetry

      Pipeline

      1. Guard: if no AprilTag pose is available yet, return AimParams.impossible().
      2. Get field-relative velocity from drivetrain. Use zero if drivetrain is not yet bound (prevents NPE during simulation startup before drivetrain is wired).
      3. LeadCompensator.computeLeadTarget(edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Pose3d, edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Pose3d, edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Translation2d, frc.robot.aiming.AimStrategy) iterates 5 times to find the virtual target pose that compensates for robot motion during ball flight. Caches result in m_lastLeadTarget for telemetry (Aiming/LeadOffsetXM/YM).
      4. ToFAim.update(edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Pose3d, edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Pose3d, edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Translation2d) computes final pitch, speed, yaw, and TOF from the virtual target distance. Called with Translation2d.kZero velocity because lead compensation was already handled by LeadCompensator.
      Returns:
      shot parameters; status is AimParams.AimStatus.Impossible when no target is available, the distance is out of range, or the required angle violates kScoringConstraints

    • periodic

      public void periodic()
      Called by the WPILib framework every 20 ms (50 Hz). Updates all control-critical state and publishes telemetry at a reduced rate to avoid loop overruns.

      Tier 1 â€” Every Loop (control-critical)

      • Game-specific data: used by the LED state machine to know which scoring windows are active for this alliance.
      • Pose refresh: fuses the latest vision estimate into the odometry pose. Runs every loop so the aiming pipeline always has the freshest position.
      • Field zone: determines ALLIANCE / NEUTRAL / OPPONENT for game-state LED feedback.
      • Turret pose: recomputes the turret's field position from the current robot pose and a fixed offset. Used as the shooter origin in the aiming pipeline.

      Tier 2 â€” 10 Hz (display only)

      SmartDashboard and NT4 struct publishes do not affect control; they only provide AdvantageScope / Shuffleboard visibility. Rate-limiting to 10 Hz reduces the NT4 update flood that caused loop overruns before Stage 0.

    • getState

      public RobotStateMachine.RobotState getState()
      Drives the LED color state machine based on match time and game-specific data, then returns the current RobotStateMachine.RobotState.

      Warning â€” side effects: This method calls setState(RobotState) (which in turn calls refreshPoseFromVision() and update(RobotState)) and mutates switching, switchingRed, switchingGreen, and exampleColor. It also writes Robot/TimeUntilSwitchSec to SmartDashboard. Do not call this method when you only want to read the state â€” call the field state directly via isActive() instead.

      LED / Scoring-Window Schedule

      The FMS game-specific message encodes which hub color is active. When the first character is 'R' or 'B', two interleaved schedules run â€” one for the alliance whose color was announced, one for the opposing alliance. At each schedule boundary a 3-second flash sequence fires (switchingRed â†’ red blink, switchingGreen â†’ green blink, switching â†’ white blink) to signal the drive team that the scoring window is changing. The flash sequences are coordinated through newPostedValue(), which is called at 10 Hz from periodic().
      Returns:
      current RobotStateMachine.RobotState after applying all state transitions

    • underTrench

      public boolean underTrench()
      Returns true when the robot is physically inside a trench run.

      The four trench regions are defined by field coordinates (meters, origin at blue alliance wall corner):

      • Blue trench top: x âˆˆ [3.7, 5.3], y âˆˆ [6.5, 8.3]
      • Blue trench bottom: x âˆˆ [3.7, 5.3], y âˆˆ [0, 1.8]
      • Red trench top: x âˆˆ [10.9, 12.8], y âˆˆ [6.5, 8.3]
      • Red trench bottom: x âˆˆ [10.9, 12.8], y âˆˆ [0, 1.8]
      Used by the flywheel to limit hood angle while passing under the trench bar.
